newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary media sell-off tenders out in two wks - ORTT.
newsitem.headline: Hungary media sell-off tenders out in two wks - ORTT.

text.p: The head of Hungary's broadcasting authority said on Saturday the long-delayed tenders for the privatisation of large chunks of the country's national media will be published within a fortnight.

"In two weeks the initial tenders will be published and in November we can finalise the applications with the bidders," Mihaly T. Revesz, head of the National Radio and Television Authority (ORTT) told a conference of potential investors.
"We expect the winners to be announced in the spring so that they can take over the running of the stations in the summer of 1997," he said.

The sale involves the presently state-owned second channel and a third channel using a currently unused frequency which used to broadcast the programmes of the former Soviet Union to around two-thirds of all homes. Two national radio frequencies are also available.

Hungary's media law, passed last December after four years of bitter political dispute, stipulated that the ORTT should invite tenders for ten-year concessions for the two television channels on June 1, with the tender results due to be announced on November 1 in time for launch on January 1.

However, inter-ministerial wranglings, government policy revisions and uncertainties over the future of broadcasting company Antenna Hungaria, which will upgrade the third frquency to increase its coverage to the whole of Hungary, have caused the process to fall way behind schedule.
This weekend's two-day conference was called by the ORTT to reassure investors that the sell-offs were on track despite the delays.

Companies lining up to bid for the television concessions include the US-based Central European Media Enterprise Group CME, the Luxemburg-based CLT which owns RTL satellite television, a Hungarian-Swedish consortium MTM- SBS and French television channel TF1.
TF1 announced earlier this week it planned to set up a consortium with German Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung (WAZ) to bid for MTV2 and said CLT and German media company Bertelsmann may join them.

Revesz admitted the timetable for privatisation set by the media law was unrealistic from the start. But he said "Once we announce the general tender in two weeks we will be on track, with no going back. The delays are over."
However, a further complication is the financial and ownership situation at Antenna Hungaria.

The state-owned broadcaster, which handles all transmissions, is reported to have debts of more than three billion forints, mainly as a result of arrears in transmission fee payments from state-owned radio and TV channels.

Efforts to privatise the company have stalled after its owner, Hungary's state privatisation agency APV, in June declared unsuccessful a new tender to sell a majority stake, rejecting a second bid by the French company Tele Diffusion de France (TDF).
TDF last week closed down their Budapest office.
On Saturday Revesz expressed his misgivings about giving a controlling stake in Antenna Hungaria, which does not fall under ORTT jurisdiction, to a foreign company.
"You don't sell your national stadium and your national team together," he said, adding that he was opposed to TDF's bid on the grounds that it is at least partly-owned by the French government.
He said there were other ways of financing the upgrade of the third channel, which he earlier estimated would cost 12 billion forints.
"APV sources or foreign bank loans are also possible -- I beleive foreign bank loans alone can solve the probably," he said.
